LESSON: ORAL EXPRESSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Oral Expression
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Expression, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 7 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: How does varied vocabulary help in effective communication? 4 (e.g. 你们家有几口人? 爷爷做什 么工作 ?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify familiar words and phrases in simple conversations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Expression in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use varied and appropriate vocabulary in oral communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Expression in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. exhibit interest in using vocabulary effectively during interactions.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Expression in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify familiar words and phrases in simple conversations,

   Oral Expression helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use varied and appropriate vocabulary in oral communication,

   Oral Expression helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. exhibit interest in using vocabulary effectively during interactions.

   Oral Expression helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. mime or gesture different professions as their peers guess the correct title and say them aloud (老 师、医生、司机、警察、护士、 农民 ),

2. listen to simple descriptions of the various professions and assign the appropriate title for each description,

3. team up with peers to sing the song on titles and professions of nuclear family members (爸爸、妈妈、哥 哥、弟弟、姐姐、妹妹、外公、 外婆、奶奶、爷爷),

4. work jointly to introduce members of their nuclear family (name, age, and profession),

5. take turns to answer questions related to the name, age, and profession of their nuclear family

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. mime or gesture different professions as their peers guess the correct title and say them aloud (老 师、医生、司机、警察、护士、 农民 ),
2. listen to simple descriptions of the various professions and assign the appropriate title for each description,
3. team up with peers to sing the song on titles and professions of nuclear family members (爸爸、妈妈、哥 哥、弟弟、姐姐、妹妹、外公、 外婆、奶奶、爷爷),
4. work jointly to introduce members of their nuclear family (name, age, and profession),
5. take turns to answer questions related to the name, age, and profession of their nuclear family

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Expression together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: the learner demonstrates tolerance and understanding of different viewpoints as they acknowledge and respect the

diverse professional aspirations of their peers.

• Communication and Collaboration: the learner speaks effectively and logically when they make short presentations of their

nuclear family members.

Values:
Unity: the learner displays team spirit as they take turns answering questions related to their nuclear family members.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Career guidance: the learner acknowledges the role their parents play in empowering and supporting them to pursue their career

aspirations.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the concept of making choices and professional aspirations to Social Studies.

Main points to remember:

1. identify familiar words and phrases in simple conversations,
2. use varied and appropriate vocabulary in oral communication,
3. exhibit interest in using vocabulary effectively during interactions.
